When a host hits the 400-URL cap, it indicates either a large archive or an inefficient traversal strategy. The BFS approach fails to capture infinite scroll or paginated structures, leading to underestimation of true surface size. Rate limiting introduces a deterministic failure mode, where 429 responses halt progress. The derived primitives formalize these behaviors into probabilistic and topological operators. The surface confirmatory primitive maps BFS reach to a confidence measure, while the coverage probability quantifies how much of a site's structure is accessible. The rate limiting primitive identifies a failure condition that impacts both GSI inference and GSE state transitions.
